extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Circulatory system organs — Heart: a muscular organ in the chest that pumps blood to the whole body, beats continuously. Arteries: blood vessels that carry blood AWAY from the heart to body parts, have thick walls. Veins: blood vessels that carry blood BACK to the heart, have valves to prevent backflow. (2) Functions of blood — carries oxygen from lungs to all body parts, carries nutrients from digested food to body cells, carries waste products away to be removed, helps fight disease and heal wounds by clotting. Red blood cells carry oxygen. White blood cells fight germs. Platelets help clotting. Plasma carries nutrients and waste. (3) Process of circulation — heart pumps blood out through arteries to all body parts. In the body, blood delivers oxygen and nutrients to cells and collects waste. Blood returns to heart through veins. Heart pumps blood to lungs to collect fresh oxygen. Cycle repeats continuously. Misconceptions: 'arteries carry blood to the heart' (WRONG — arteries carry blood AWAY from the heart, veins carry blood back TO the heart), 'veins are red because they carry oxygen' (WRONG — veins appear blue because they carry deoxygenated blood back to the heart; arteries are red because they carry oxygen-rich blood), 'the heart is on the left side of the chest' (PARTIALLY WRONG — the heart is in the center of the chest but tilted slightly to the left), 'blood only carries oxygen' (WRONG — blood also carries nutrients, waste, and helps fight disease and clot wounds), 'veins have valves just for decoration' (WRONG — valves prevent backflow of blood, especially important in legs where blood must flow upward against gravity).
